resources.string: Course 3 · Advanced. 18 holes in the autumn highlands: golden grass, pines, rocks and cold lakes. Narrow landing shelves reward driver and wood carries, then precise hops between banks. The broad route remains the conservative choice.

string-array.name: classic_wild_tips
string-array.item: The broad left fairway is safe. A driver to the right clearing, about 232 m from the tee, leaves a shorter approach. Avoid the central ridge.
Follow the broad right bank, or carry a driver to the 225 m landing beyond the first lake. A wood 3 then jumps about 205 m across the second lake to the final shelf.
Water guards the entrance. An iron 5 covers the theoretical 155 m; the right apron is a bailout, while rear sand punishes excess distance.
The broad left elbow is safe. A driver can reach the small right saddle at about 227 m, opening the uphill approach. The ridge blocks the centre shortcut.
A driver carry of about 229 m clears the diagonal lake to the left cape and leaves a wedge. The right shelf builds the hole without that long crossing.
Three left landings: driver to the first at 220 m, iron 8 for the next 116 m hop, then pitching wedge for about 97 m. The right fairway avoids these small targets.
A wood 5 covers the theoretical 186 m. The high right apron opens a diagonal entrance; the bunker guards a short left landing.
The left fairway skirts the quarry. A driver of about 227 m reaches the small right tongue beyond the sand and shortens the approach.
The broad right S is conservative. A driver of about 226 m to the left landing cuts the detour; central pines block the direct line.
The descent adds carry. The small left landing is about 228 m from the tee: use the preview to control the driver. The broad right bank gives more margin.
The left detour is broad. A driver to the right clearing at about 232 m leaves less distance to the green, provided you stay beside the forest.
A hybrid covers the theoretical 170 m. Carry the front lake without rolling into rear sand; the right apron offers more depth.
Go broad left, aim a driver at the right tongue at 229 m, or use a wood 3 to the central 210 m pocket between bunkers. Sand beyond the centre then demands a change of angle.
A driver of about 229 m reaches the right balcony and cuts the detour. The left bank is broader; the final shot still climbs to the green.
Driver to the left cape at about 230 m, then wood 3 to the second cape at 202 m. Those landings leave an iron to the green; the broad right bank allows three conservative shots.
A wood 3 covers the theoretical 205 m. Right water and left sand frame the green; the front-left apron preserves a chip option.
The left shelf is broad. A driver of about 224 m reaches the small right landing between ridge and lake and opens a more direct approach.
Driver to the 220 m pocket beyond the first lake, then wood 3 for 210 m to the final landing. The broad right crescent avoids those two precise crossings.
